title: Signal-Triggered Escalation from Local MLX Agent Loop to Haiku vs Local-Only vs Always-Haiku
target_platform: Apple Silicon M1 (16GB) local Qwen2.5-Coder-7B loop + Claude Haiku 5.5 via cli-agent
hypothesis: Escalating a task from the local MLX agent loop to Claude Haiku when a loop-health trigger fires (no final answer, >=4 turns, repeat intervention, malformed reply, or forced final turn) reaches >=95% correct on generated held-out repository-discovery tasks while escalating <=35% of tasks, beating both local-only (73-83% in MISSION-022) and always-Haiku on cost-adjusted accuracy.
falsification_criteria: Escalate-on-signal correct rate < 95%, or escalation rate > 35%, or always-Haiku is both cheaper (credits + wall-clock) and >= as accurate, or the trigger misses > 20% of local failures (silent confident errors such as MISSION-022 D9/D10 are expected misses and need a verifier; see MISSION-007).
baseline_evidence: MISSION-022 runs 4+5 (60 tasks): local correct 47/60; the trigger flags 19/60, catching 10/13 failures; 9 of the 19 flagged tasks were already correct (wasted escalations); 3 misses were silent directory-listing errors; locate tier is the weak one (10 of 13 failures).

model_routing.frontier_escalation_condition: This mission measures the escalation policy itself; escalate to Haiku only through the signal trigger under test.

projected_impact.basis: Declared 2026-11-04 by claude-code (MISSION-031 backfill) from the mission's hypothesis; a mission always also edits its own manifest. Refine at checkout and confirm with `manage_coordination.py verify`.
